== Overview ==
Kinomiya Faith is widely distributed along the {{ill|Sagami Bay|ar|خليج ساغامي|ca|Badia de Sagami|ceb|Sagami-wan|da|Sagamibugten|de|Sagami-Bucht|es|Bahía de Sagami|eu|Sagami Badia|fa|خلیج ساگامی|fr|Baie de Sagami|he|מפרץ סגאמי|hy|Սագամի ծովածոց|id|Teluk Sagami|it|Baia di Sagami|ja|相模湾|ko|사가미만|lt|Sagamio įlanka|nl|Sagamibaai|no|Sagamibukta|pl|Sagami (zatoka)|pt|Baía de Sagami|ru|Сагами (залив)|simple|Sagami Bay|th|อ่าวซางามิ|tr|Sagami Körfezi|uk|Саґамська затока|vi|Vịnh Sagami|zh|相模灣|qid=Q1061221}} coastal area, from western {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|qid=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}} to {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|en|Shizuoka Prefecture|qid=Q131320|lt=Shizuoka Prefecture}}'s {{ill|Izu Peninsula|en|Izu Peninsula|qid=Q822822|lt=Izu Peninsula}}. It primarily centers around shrines named "Kinomiya." The name Kinomiya is variously written as '''Kinomiya''' (木宮), '''Kinomiya''' (貴宮), '''Kinomiya''' (来宮), '''Kinomiya''' (黄宮), '''Kinomiya''' (木野宮), '''Kinomiya''' (紀伊宮), among others. The enshrined deities vary but frequently involve tree spirits or {{ill|driftwood deities|ja|漂着神}}. Its distribution overlaps significantly with areas known for the {{ill|kashima odo|ja|鹿島踊り|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11677163}} dance.

There are multiple theories regarding the origin of the name Kinomiya:
*'''"Ki-no-Miya" (来の宮) Theory''' – Shrines situated along coasts, often founded around driftwood deities (gods that "arrived" from the sea).
*'''"Ki-no-Miya" (木の宮) Theory''' – Derives from {{ill|tree worship|ja|樹木信仰|qid=Q1425797}} or the faith of the {{ill|Kijiya|en|Kijiya|qid=Q11518247|lt=Kijishi woodworkers}}.
*'''"Ki-no-Miya" (忌の宮) Theory''' – Based on {{ill|Abstinence rituals|ja|忌み|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5857008}} observed during ceremonies.
*'''"Ki-no-Miya" (紀の宮) Theory''' – Related to gods from {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}, such as {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|qid=Q3200355}}, though "Kii" itself likely stems from the character for tree (木), thus possibly an extension of the "tree shrine" theory.

The lack of consensus is attributed to the faith's composite nature, involving aspects like driftwood shrines, tree worship, and unclear origins.

== Shrines of Kinomiya Faith ==
Notable shrines include:
*'''{{ill|Kii Shrine|ja|紀伊神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q112042855}}''' (Hayakawa, Odawara, Kanagawa) – Formerly Kii-no-Miya/Kinomiya Daigongen, enshrining Itakeru-no-Mikoto and Prince Koretaka.
*'''{{ill|Kifune Shrine (Manazuru, Kanagawa)|ja|貴船神社 (真鶴町)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11634812}}''' (Manazuru, Ashigarashimo, Kanagawa) – Former district shrine known as Kimiyamiya Daimyōjin, enshrining Ōkuninushi, Kotoshironushi, and Sukunahikona.
*'''{{ill|Kinomiya Shrine|ja|来宮神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11523682}}''' (Nishiyama, Atami, Shizuoka) – Former Village shrine, currently a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine}}, enshrining Itakeru-no-Mikoto.
*'''{{ill|Kinomiya Shrine (Q119929624)|ja|来宮神社 (伊豆市八幡)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q119929624}}''' (Izushi, Shizuoka) – Former district shrine, enshrining Itakeru-no-Mikoto.
*'''{{ill|Hachimangū Kinomiya Shrine|ja|八幡宮来宮神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11390944}}''' (Hachimanno, Itō, Shizuoka) – Former district shrine, Kinomiya Shrine merged into a {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman Shrine}}, enshrining Iwakura Wake-no-Mikoto.
*'''{{ill|Shiritaogi Shrine|ja|志理太乎宜神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q134892415}}''' (Shirata, Higashiizu, Shizuoka) – Former Village shrine, potential {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q1342448}}, enshrining Itakeru-no-Mikoto.
*'''{{ill|Sugihokowake no Mikoto Shrine|ja|川津来宮神社|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 杉桙別命神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11522170}} ({{ill|Sugihokowake no Mikoto Shrine|ja|杉桙別命神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11522170}})''' (Tanaka, Kawazu, Shizuoka) – Shikinaisha, former district shrine known as Kinomiya/Myōjin, enshrining Sugihokowake-no-Mikoto.

Additionally, many shrines within this area, while not explicitly named Kinomiya, also worship tree or driftwood deities and have unique abstinence rituals.

Historically, in the {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県#地域区分|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q131358}} within {{ill|Shiga District, Shiga|en|Shiga District, Shiga|qid=Q7496289|lt=Shiga District, Ōmi Province}}, a practice called '''Kinomiya Shōjin''' (季宮精進) occurred specifically on {{ill|November 23 (Lunisolar)|ja|11月23日 (旧暦)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q840512}} to prevent fires by refraining from unnecessary fire usage and not consuming cooked food throughout the day. This practice is considered related to Kinomiya Faith<ref>『神道大辞典』, Heibonsha, 1937.</ref>.
